title: Keep the month-end reconciliation fast as volume grows

blocks.text: At month end the warehouse reconciles what it shipped against what finance billed. The step that finds the unbilled lines took a few seconds when the business was small; now each month is several times larger than the last, and the step's run time grows much faster than the month.

`Reconciler` already prints the report line. Finish `unbilled(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Reconciler.java`: it returns the shipped items that are not among the billed ones, in shipping order, with repeats, and changes neither input. Items are compared with `equals()` and `hashCode()`; they are not `Comparable`.
When you're done, doubling both inputs roughly doubles the work this method does. About five lines in total.
The tests use items that count the `equals()` and `hashCode()` calls made on them.

cases.says: the unbilled items come back in shipping order, repeats included, and neither input list changes
with nothing billed every shipped item is unbilled, and the summary line counts them
the work per shipped item does not grow with the number of billed items: equals() calls stay a small multiple of the input size
the lookup structure over the billed items is built once, so hashCode() calls stay a small multiple of the input size

origin.section: A Call Inside a Loop Multiplies: List.contains in a Loop Is O(n²)

concepts: List.contains scans, so calling it once per element of a loop is O(n^2); a HashSet built once before the loop keeps the loop O(n), and building it inside the loop is quadratic again.
